question: Point P on a number line represents -2. Move P 5 unit lengths to the right to obtain point Q. What number does Q represent?
solution: Moving to the right means adding: \(-2+5=3\).

nodes.label: 6.NS.C.6c

nodes.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend number line diagrams and coordinate axes familiar from previous grades to represent points on the line and in the plane with negative number coordinates.
nodes.label: 6.NS.C.6

nodes.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line diagram by defining the interval from 0 to 1 as the whole and partitioning it into b equal parts. Recognize that each part has size 1/b and that the endpoint of the part based at 0 locates the number 1/b on the number line.
nodes.label: 3.NF.A.2a

nodes.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, ..., and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram .
nodes.label: 2.MD.B.6

nodes.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line diagram by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0. Recognize that the resulting interval has size a/b and that its endpoint locates the number a/b on the number line.
nodes.label: 3.NF.A.2b

nodes.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100. For example, rewrite 0.62 as 62/100; describe a length as 0.62 meters; locate 0.62 on a number line diagram . *Grade 4 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, and 100.
nodes.label: 4.NF.C.6

nodes.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram . *Grade 3 expectations in this domain are limited to fractions with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8.
nodes.label: 3.NF.A.2

nodes.description: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, with the intersection of the lines (the origin) arranged to coincide with the 0 on each line and a given point in the plane located by using an ordered pair of numbers, called its coordinates. Understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin in the direction of one axis, and the second number indicates how far to travel in the direction of the second axis, with the convention that the names of the two axes and the coordinates correspond (e.g., x-axis and x-coordinate, y-axis and y-coordinate).
nodes.label: 5.G.A.1

edges.reason: The actual number-line criterion checks an origin, a designated direction and a unit. A designated positive direction is an orientation convention; it does not require the full signed-number classification or negative contexts asserted by Gemini.
edges.scope: Origin, designated orientation and unit as the three structural elements of a number line

edges.reason: Formal rational-number taxonomy identifies the domain of examples but plotting a given signed fraction or decimal only needs its value and the axis; classification is useful preparation.
To place or read a number on the axis one must interpret its origin, unit and positive direction.
edges.scope: Plotting and reading points on a number line

edges.reason: Gains/losses provide a meaningful model of signed addition, while the formal sign-and-magnitude rule can be learned abstractly; retain useful preparation.
The specified signed-addition rule compares and adds/subtracts absolute values. This is necessity for that rule, not for every possible addition model.
edges.scope: Stating and applying the formal addition rule
